Cape Sagan-Khushun & the Three Brothers Rock, Russia 🇷🇺🏔✨

On the western shore of Olkhon Island, Cape Sagan-Khushun rises above Lake Baikal, its luminous white cliffs carving a dramatic silhouette against the sky. Here, the Three Brothers Rock stands tall — three colossal stone pillars steeped in legend.

According to Buryat folklore, these rocks were once brothers, turned to stone while defending their sister from a vengeful shaman. The tale lingers in the wind, lending the place an air of mystery and timeless strength — as if the earth still honors their sacrifice.

Battered by winds and breathtaking in scale, Sagan-Khushun remains one of Lake Baikal’s most sacred and stunning sites — where myth, nature, and eternity converge.

🔊 Iran hold Egypt to draw, keep World Cup hopes alive

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s national football team drew 1-1 with Egypt in its final Group G match of the 2026 FIFA World Cup on Saturday, remaining unbeaten after three consecutive draws while keeping hopes of advancing to the knockout stage as one of the tournament's best third-placed teams.

Played in Seattle, the match saw Egypt take an early lead in the fifth minute through Mahmoud Saber. Iran had a golden opportunity to equalize five minutes later when Mehdi Taremi won a penalty, but goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir denied his effort.
​
Iran responded quickly in the 14th minute as Ramin Rezaeian converted the rebound after Milad Mohammadi’s shot was saved, leveling the score at 1-1.
​
The second half was largely controlled by Egypt, although Iran remained dangerous on the counterattack. Egypt substituted star forward Mohamed Salah in the 56th minute, while Iranian goalkeeper Alireza Beiranvand produced several important saves to keep his side in the match.
​
Iran came close to claiming victory in stoppage time. Shoja Khalilzadeh found the net in the 93rd minute, but the goal was ruled out for offside after a VAR review. Four minutes later, Saeid Ezatolahi’s header struck the crossbar.
​
The result left Iran third in Group G with three points from three draws. Belgium topped the group with five points, while Egypt also finished on five points but with an inferior goal difference. Iran must now await results from other groups to determine whether it qualifies among the best third-placed teams.

Crypto Idea

The boldest experiment in crypto

Michael Saylor, the founder of Strategy, the world's largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, has come up with something unique.

Instead of simply buying Bitcoin with the company's own money, he's building an entire financial machine that attracts outside capital and channels it into BTC purchases.

One of these instruments is STRC. Investors provide capital to the company and receive regular payouts of around 11.5% annually. The company then uses that capital to buy Bitcoin. But there's a catch.

⚙️ How it’s supposed to work

STRC — an instrument Saylor designed with the help of AI — is intended to keep its price hovering around $100.

If the price falls, the company raises the yield to attract more buyers. The price is supposed to recover. Think of it as an automatic stabilizer.

❓ Why this is interesting 

Right now, STRC is trading at roughly $83, despite its $100 target value. The yield has already been increased, but the market isn't responding the way the model was designed to.

This is the first real stress test of the entire structure. If the mechanism fails to stabilize the price, the company will either have to keep increasing payouts to investors or buy less Bitcoin.

Saylor is essentially testing one question: can financial instruments be built around a single asset indefinitely?
